trip.title: Southwest Loop — January
trip.subtitle: Death Valley · Zion · Page · Monument Valley · Grand Canyon · Route 66
trip.start_end: Las Vegas, NV (Harry Reid International — LAS)
trip.summary: A counterclockwise loop out of Las Vegas taking in five national parks and one Navajo tribal park. Warm start in Death Valley, a cold middle at elevation, and an easy Route 66 run home. Two versions are priced: a motorhome build and a car-plus-hotels build.

itinerary.headline: Below sea level by lunchtime
itinerary.notes: Pick up the vehicle and drive straight in. Furnace Creek sits 190 feet below sea level and is the warmest place you'll sleep all trip — January highs around 18°C, lows around 4°C.

itinerary.headline: The valley floor
itinerary.notes: Badwater Basin is the lowest point in North America. Artist's Drive is a one-way loop through mineral-stained hills and is limited to vehicles under 25 feet.

itinerary.headline: Dunes and craters
itinerary.notes: Ubehebe Crater is a 110-mile round trip from Furnace Creek. Dante's View sits at 5,475 feet and can be 14°C colder than the valley floor — it also caps at 25 feet.

itinerary.to: Valley of Fire State Park, NV
itinerary.headline: Back through Vegas to the red rock
itinerary.notes: Nevada's oldest state park. Bright red Aztec sandstone, petroglyphs, and short walks that suit kids. All campsites are now reservation-only.

itinerary.headline: Into the canyon
itinerary.notes: Enter Zion from the south at Springdale. In winter the park shuttle does not run, which means you can drive Zion Canyon Scenic Drive yourself — a road closed to private vehicles most of the year.

itinerary.headline: Full day in Zion
itinerary.notes: Canyon floor is around 4,000 feet — 10 to 12°C days, −2°C nights. The mildest of the cold stops.

itinerary.headline: The long way round to Lake Powell
itinerary.notes: Routed via Hurricane, Colorado City and Kanab. An RV cannot take the direct Mount Carmel Highway through the tunnel — see vehicle_restrictions.

itinerary.headline: Horseshoe Bend, then the Navajo Nation
itinerary.notes: Horseshoe Bend is $10 per vehicle and a 1.5-mile round-trip walk — far better value than a guided slot canyon tour.

itinerary.headline: Sunrise over the Mittens
itinerary.notes: The 17-mile Tribal Park Loop is unpaved and closed to RVs and motorcycles by Navajo Nation rules. In a car you can drive it yourself. The Wildcat Trail is a free 3.2-mile loop around West Mitten Butte from the visitor center.

itinerary.headline: In through the East Entrance
itinerary.notes: Via Kayenta, Tuba City and Cameron. Coming in from the east means you pass Desert View Watchtower before reaching the village — the better approach.

itinerary.headline: The rim
itinerary.notes: Coldest night of the trip — highs around 5°C, lows around −8°C. Free park shuttles run year-round. Snow on the rim over red rock, and the park at its emptiest all year.

itinerary.headline: Route 66 westbound
itinerary.notes: The Seligman-to-Kingman stretch is the longest intact original section of Route 66 left. Do not take the Oatman Highway — Sitgreaves Pass is steep with blind hairpins and most rental agreements prohibit it.

itinerary.headline: Short day home
itinerary.notes: Deliberately light. This is the weather buffer — if snow costs you a day earlier in the trip, you absorb it here.

itinerary.headline: A last day in Las Vegas
itinerary.notes: A free day before the Saturday flight home — and a second spare day if snow cost you one earlier in the trip.

itinerary.headline: Fly home
itinerary.notes: The Saturday flight home. Anything still rented goes back at the airport on the way in.

options.name: Motorhome

vehicle.notes: Book by seatbelt count, not sleeping capacity. The smaller C25 measures 24.93 ft long, 8.33 ft wide and 12.20 ft high — it clears Death Valley's 25-foot roads but is still too wide and too tall for Zion's Mount Carmel Highway.

best_location.why: Inside the park. You wake up at Furnace Creek and reach Zabriskie Point for sunrise in ten minutes.

best_value.why: Thirty minutes to the park's northeast entrance, an hour to Furnace Creek. Saves close to $1,000 over three nights — the single biggest lever in the whole budget.

best_location.why: Walking distance to the park entrance. January is low season, so Springdale is unusually affordable.

best_value.price_per_night: $200-280 for a whole house; $70-90 per motel room
best_value.why: The best rental-house stop on the route. A kitchen here meaningfully cuts the food line.

best_location.why: Lake views. Worth it only if you want the view; otherwise Page town is fine.

picks: Page chain hotels — Hampton, Best Western, Rodeway
best_value.why: Page is genuinely cheap in winter. No reason to overspend on a single night.

best_location.why: Every room faces the Mittens. If you splurge once on this trip, splurge here — you wake up to the view rather than driving to it.

best_value.why: Kayenta is 25 minutes out, Goulding's 10 minutes. Goulding's is the middle ground on both price and position.

best_location.why: Inside the park, walking distance to the rim, free shuttles year-round.

best_value.why: The value pick and the location pick are the same here. Tusayan hotels seven miles outside run $109-135 — no cheaper than staying in the park. Book in-park.

vehicle_restrictions.location: Zion — Mount Carmel Highway and tunnel
vehicle_restrictions.rule: As of 7 June 2026 the oversized-vehicle escort was eliminated entirely. Any vehicle over the limits is banned from the whole stretch between Canyon Junction and the East Entrance. No permit, escort or exception exists.
vehicle_restrictions.impact_on_rv: Blocked. Every Class C is roughly 8 ft wide and 12 ft tall regardless of length, so downsizing does not help. Reroute via Hurricane, Colorado City and Kanab.
vehicle_restrictions.impact_on_car: None. Any car, minivan or standard SUV can drive it in any season.

vehicle_restrictions.location: Death Valley — Artist's Drive and the final climb to Dante's View
vehicle_restrictions.impact_on_rv: A 30-footer is blocked. A C25 measures 24.93 ft — a three-inch margin, so measure the actual unit at pickup.

vehicle_restrictions.rule: The Navajo Nation prohibits RVs and motorcycles on the loop drive. The road is unpaved with washboard and deep sand.
vehicle_restrictions.impact_on_rv: Blocked by category, not by size. Free alternatives: the visitor center overlook and the 3.2-mile Wildcat Trail. A Navajo-guided 4x4 tour runs $70-95 per person.
vehicle_restrictions.impact_on_car: None — drive it yourself, included in the tribal park entry fee.

vehicle_restrictions.location: Route 66 — Oatman Highway over Sitgreaves Pass
vehicle_restrictions.rule: Steep with blind hairpins. Most rental agreements effectively prohibit it.
vehicle_restrictions.impact_on_rv: Avoid. Stay on the Seligman-to-Kingman section instead.

money_savers.detail: Lower Antelope now costs $80.50 per person plus a $15 Navajo permit — about $580 for six. Upper runs $115-140 per person. The famous light beams only appear between 11am and 1pm from March to October, so in January you would pay peak-adjacent prices for a canyon without its main feature.
A 1.5-mile round-trip walk, no tour, no permit. $10 total for the whole group.
A genuine slot canyon you walk yourself on BLM land, about 90 minutes from Page toward Kanab. The access road is dirt and turns to slop when wet.

money_savers.item: Sleep in Beatty, not in the park
money_savers.detail: The largest single lever in the car-and-hotels build.
Buy bedding and kitchen gear at a Las Vegas store on day one for $200-300 and leave it behind. Cheaper than per-person kit fees for six.
Covers Death Valley, Zion, Grand Canyon and Glen Canyon. It does NOT cover Monument Valley, which is a Navajo tribal park, or Valley of Fire, which is a Nevada state park.

practical_notes.cold_weather: Seven nights at or below freezing in the motorhome build — Zion, Page, Monument Valley and the Grand Canyon. Every one of those stops has a full-hookup option. Run the propane furnace, not the heat pump, which stops working around 4°C. Disconnect the city water hose at night and run off the fresh tank; the hose freezes long before the tanks.
practical_notes.rental_freeze_risk: Rental companies push freeze damage onto the renter and treat a burst pipe as negligent damage at full repair cost. Confirm in writing that the unit is not winterized, that the water system is live, and that they have noted your cold-weather destinations on the booking.
practical_notes.booking_order: Grand Canyon lodging or Trailer Village first, then Goulding's or The View at Monument Valley, then Watchman at Zion. Those three set the skeleton — everything else has slack.
practical_notes.mileage_fees: If the rental charges per mile at around $0.35, 1,655 miles adds roughly $580. Always price the unlimited-miles package as an alternative.
practical_notes.fuel: Fill up in Nevada, Utah and Arizona. Top off before entering Death Valley, where in-park fuel at Furnace Creek is notably expensive.
practical_notes.death_valley_closures: Flood damage persists. Bonnie Clare Road and Scotty's Castle are closed with no reopening date, North Highway has loose gravel and missing shoulders, southern Badwater Road has soft shoulders and unpaved sections, and Emigrant Campground is closed indefinitely. Check the park's conditions page a week before departure.
practical_notes.buffer: Day 13 is deliberately short, and day 14 is a free day in Las Vegas before the flight. If snow costs you a day earlier in the trip, there are two places to absorb it.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Strong park, but it sits on the opposite side of the map from Monument Valley. Cannot have both in two weeks.
The warmest and most kid-friendly stop available, but on the western route only.
No hookups, no potable water, no cell service, and the York Fire burned close to 100,000 acres in 2023 including much of the Cima Dome Joshua tree forest.
In January the lake is too cold to swim, which removes the main reason to go. London Bridge is a ten-minute stop.

rejected_alternatives.place: Saguaro NP and Lost Dutchman SP
rejected_alternatives.reason: Both good, but adding them means a 400-mile I-10 leg — the worst driving day in any version of this trip.
Sits at 8,000 feet. Genuinely miserable in January.
Trailer rentals do not include a tow vehicle, and the major rental companies prohibit towing outright. Turo treats towing as a prohibited use that voids damage protection.
